title: Subtraction of 3-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Subtraction – Primary 3 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Subtract 3-digit numbers with and without exchanging (borrowing); check subtraction by addition. (summary of the NERDC Primary 3 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 maths worksheets on subtracting 3-digit numbers with and without exchanging, column subtraction and checking by addition. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Take away units, then tens, then hundreds
key_sub: Not enough? Exchange 1 ten for 10 units.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Write the bigger number on top and line up the columns.
  • Start with the units. If the top digit is smaller, exchange 1 ten for 10 units.
  • Check by adding: the answer + the number taken away = the first number.

Examples

Example

532 − 178

Exchange: 12 − 8 = 4

12 − 7 = 5 (after exchanging a hundred)

4 − 1 = 3

Answer: 354

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Taking the smaller digit from the bigger digitIn 52 − 18 you cannot do 8 − 2; exchange instead.
Forgetting the exchanged tenCross out and write one less.
Putting the smaller number on topThe bigger number goes on top.

faq.q: What is the difference between two numbers?
faq.a: The answer when you subtract the smaller from the bigger.
Add your answer to the number you took away.

faq.q: Can I subtract in any order?
faq.a: No. 9 − 4 is not the same as 4 − 9.

items.q: Use the blocks. What is 147 + 6?
items.e: There are 7 + 6 = 13 cubes. Exchange 10 cubes for 1 rod: 4 tens become 5 tens, and 3 units are left. 147 + 6 = 153.

items.q: Jump to the next ten first. What is 347 + 6?

items.q: Which calculation checks 523 − 178 = 345?
items.e: Addition is the inverse of subtraction. Add the answer to the number you took away: 345 + 178 = 523. That is the number you started with, so the answer is right.

items.q: Round each number to the nearest hundred. Which is the best estimate for 386 + 247?
items.e: 386 rounds to 400 and 247 rounds to 200. 400 + 200 = 600. The exact answer is 633, which is close to 600.
